packs.title: Color beyond the Strip
packs.promise: Find the city in working art spaces, civic buildings and outdoor forms.

q.s: Find three different rhythms on one public-facing block.
st: Choose a public-sidewalk view outside gallery doors and loading areas.
Find a repeated window or doorway shape, a broad surface, and one small contrasting detail.
Record the three rhythms and choose which gives the building the strongest visual beat.

q.s: Find three connections between a structure and the sun.
st: Choose an open public-sidewalk or plaza viewpoint outside security and event boundaries.
Find a solar-panel surface, a supporting stem and the patch of ground beneath it.
Describe the relationship among those three parts without needing sunlight or a working display.

q.s: Collect three gestures from a material that seems rigid.
st: Find an open public path viewpoint outside any reserved event.
Choose a curl, a pinch and an open space in the sculpture’s steel forms.
Give each form a movement word, then choose the word that best fits the whole work.

packs.title: Impossible Worlds
packs.promise: Find the small surprises inside the city’s biggest illusions.

q.s: Give a fountain performance its own beginning, middle, and ending.
st: Check the operator’s current fountain schedule and choose a permitted sidewalk viewing point with room for others to pass.
During a performance, notice three different water shapes or movements. Follow the visual changes even if you cannot hear the music.
Choose the moment that feels like a beginning, the strongest change, and the ending you would remember. They can be simple rises, curves, or pauses.
Save your three acts as short descriptions or photograph one moment. If no performance happens, complete the still-scene alternative.

q.s: Make one image or description hold an unlikely pair.
st: From a clear public sidewalk viewpoint near the Bellagio lake, find two things that seem to belong to different worlds: water and stone, a decorative facade and glass tower, or something else visible.
Choose a frame that gives each thing room. Stay in one place or make only a small safe adjustment; crossing the road is unnecessary.
Invent a one-sentence description connecting the pair without pretending the buildings are in the places they imitate.
Save the image or write the composition and your sentence in a field note. No iconic landmark has to fit in the frame.

q.s: Watch the architecture rearrange itself along a short elevated ride.
st: At Bellagio, follow current signs for the ARIA Express Tram. Check service and the accessible route to the platform before committing to the trip.
Board toward the ARIA/Park MGM end of the route when directed. Once settled, notice one close surface, one distant building, and one transition where their relationship changes.
Exit at the station serving ARIA/Park MGM and clear the platform before writing. Use signs toward Park MGM and The Park if you continue the chapter.
Save the three observations and your favorite transition. The stationary alternative completes the same quest if a ride does not suit you.
